what: Before the Round 16 model change the builder copied the old RDBMS model (base5-rdbms_postgresql.model) and ran pg_dump to dump-before-r16.sql (8.3 MB) so that the existing data could be migrated, not wiped.
why: schema-upgrade applies generate and execute in one step, so no hand-written backfill can be inserted; the documented route is generate, backfill, then execute.

what: The review round (no code changes) discarded the unsaved model edits left by the aborted build with judo-cli discard --force, rather than saving them, so that the model matched e35dddd.
why: The review round forbids model or code changes; the dirty edits were partial and unreviewed.

what: Customer rows are provisioned by a hand-written CustomerProvisioningInterceptor on the first customer-client login, and Admin rows are not created automatically. The reason given is the catalog's gotcha that the runtime does lookup only, not first-login insert.
why: The access-point and authentication pages state that managed/claim actors are looked up and a missing row raises AUTHENTICATED_ENTITY_NOT_FOUND; the interceptor must insert the row.

what: Used the documented route schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade after a pg_dump backup. It finished in 36 s, added the new columns and a stock reservation table, and kept 308 orders. This route failed in R6 and R10 according to GAPS; it worked this round.
why: The catalog now documents the route (schema-evolution.md 'When No Manual Step Is Needed'); the builder confirmed it on the running database.

what: The payment webhook is a static operation on the Admin actor (hidden access 'gateway'), called with a bearer token of a technical admin user plus an HMAC signature. An anonymous SYSTEM actor was tried first but made the admin build fail (c12-15).
why: A truly anonymous public endpoint was the catalog's answer, but the third actor broke the build; the Admin route was the least-bad documented option.
workaround: Admin access with DERIVED 0..1 getter ShopConfig!any(); webhook route POST /api/webshop/Admin/PaymentGatewayInfo/receive.

what: The payment provider is an enum on the existing shop settings row (ShopConfig.paymentProvider: STUB_SUCCEED, STUB_FAIL, STUB_TIMEOUT, HTTP). PaymentService picks the adapter from that setting; deployment values come from system properties or environment variables.
why: The catalog gives the adapter pattern but no recipe for a provider an admin can switch at runtime.
workaround: Settings row enum plus PaymentAdapter interface with stub and HTTP adapters.

what: The clock is a parameter, not a global: ReservationService.releaseExpired(LocalDateTime now). The admin button 'Release expired reservations' takes a Minutes input that moves the clock for that run, so the browser test does not sleep.
why: BusinessClock is read once at class load and cannot be changed by a browser test; the catalog has no page for a clock a running app can move.
workaround: Scheduled job passes BusinessClock.now(); tests pass any date.

what: Customer lists become card containers: 22 cards configuration hooks registered (product list, orders, returns, returnable items, notifications, addresses, company members and invitations, quotes, sub-orders, wallet gift cards and points, seller entries, reviews, exchange rates), with a shared ShopCard, status colour map, ListBars toolbar and ProductCard at 4:3 image ratio.
why: One consistent look across the customer app, and generated paging and data loading stay in the generated container.

what: Model changes for R16U: representationComponent=card on about 12 TransferObjectTables (orders, returns, returnable items, notifications, addresses, quotes, seller products, sub-orders, exchange rates, admin orders, admin returns, admin quotes) and on relation tables (wallet gift cards and points, and others), rowsPerPage 12, and customImplementation=true on 93 view fields; validate then save, then generate and build -f -i.
why: Cards need the table representation set, and the custom elements need the model mark before generation.

what: Detail screens (orders, quotes, sub-orders, returns, wallet, seller, company, notifications) get one summary layout (DetailLayout with detailSpecs) rendered by the first custom element of each view; the other fields render nothing, and a GlobalStyles rule hides their empty grid cells.
why: Keeps the generated view page (title, back, actions, relation cards) and gives a summary header with sections.

what: Customer lists are cards through the cards container hook; the detail views are custom visual elements with a summary and sections; relation lists are custom RelationCards instead of the generated relation container.
why: The generated relation cards container cannot refresh (R16U-2), so a custom element loads its own rows.

what: The model's DataColumn sort replaces the UI-side sort hack in ListBars: sort DESC on orderedAt of the orders, requestedAt of quotes and returns, and name ASC for products.
why: Model default sort is the documented place; the UI hack applied only on first load.

what: The shop card grid uses sm 6 (two columns on a tablet) instead of sm 12, because the builder found the catalog example gave one 700 px card at sm. The catalog grid example shows xs 12, md 6, lg 4 with no sm.
why: Visual result on the 768 px screenshot.
workaround: CARD_CELL changed in ShopCard.tsx for customer and admin.

what: Profile form, all operation input forms, the shop settings view and admin plain CRUD tables stay generated; only lists and detail views were converted.
why: Editing forms need the generated validation and error messages; plain CRUD tables are not in the custom UI rule.

what: The scheduled work is an OSGi scheduler (ShopScheduler and ReservationJob, own executor) that calls modeled static operations (ShopJobs: releaseExpired, syncCarrier, sendMails, remindCarts, processImport) through the Dispatcher, so each runs in a transaction. The admin buttons run the same work with an optional minutes input, so tests never sleep.
why: Platform has no scheduler; the agent-docs Scheduled Work section says to use Dispatcher.callOperation for modeled ops.

what: Order mails are sent by an OrderMails post-call trigger from each operation that changes an order, not by interceptors, because interceptors do not run around custom operations.
why: catalog platform-email-template-service says interceptors fire only on built-in operations.

what: Carrier and mail are stubs behind one interface each, switched by shop settings (STUB_SUCCEED, STUB_FAIL, STUB_TIMEOUT). The timeout stub throws at once and nothing sleeps.
why: Pattern from the external API adapter practice; tests need succeed, fail and timeout.

what: Local mail: a Mailpit container on port 1025 and judo-karaf.env SMTP variables; JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER set to false.
why: Catalog says for local testing point SMTP at localhost:1025 in judo-karaf.env.

what: Adding to the cart resets the reminder marker (cartReminderSentAt) so that a new quiet period starts; the reminder job sends at most one mail per cart.
why: A reminder belongs to the old cart content.

what: Land raw carrier status in a staging entity first, then process only new statuses.
why: Catalog pattern for external system data.

what: Own limit: cart touch only on add-to-cart and checkout; quantity edit and remove-line not treated as touch in this round.
why: Time; the interceptor route was not built.

what: Seed the 50 000 products directly into PostgreSQL instead of through the API.
why: Speed of the volume seed; no catalog entry used.

what: Facet counts and aggregates use native SQL in one isolated service (CatalogSearch), because the DAO has no aggregate method.
why: Catalog says no DAO aggregate; native SQL only via JDBC DataSource.

what: Versioning is a convention: each version a full copy grouped by a container, one approved at a time.
why: Catalog says the platform has no versioning feature.

what: GDPR delete repoints kept references to one placeholder user, then hard-deletes the real user.
why: Catalog pattern: keep authored content, drop the person.

what: Reports: aggregation in native SQL in a custom service (ReportService), one answer for table, chart and PDF; PDF from MarkdownPdf.
why: DAO cannot group; the catalog documents native SQL from a custom service.

what: Push built as a stub provider switched by a shop setting; browser polls every 4 s; real Web Push not built.
why: No push service available in the build; the blueprint names the pipeline.

what: Backfill changeset (06_updateDataAfterIncremental) hand-written inside the generated migration folder; the orchestrator rule says never patch generated files, while the best practice says write it in the generated version folder.
why: Catalog says the generator overwrites the output folder except review files; survival of a hand-written changeset is marked verify.
workaround: Changeset kept; re-check after each regeneration.

what: Compose app container runs the Karaf offline distribution of this build (copied into deploy/karaf), not a Docker image, because build -d failed.
why: Image build did not work (see c17-37).

what: Put the Guest actor first in the model (create --index 0) so the generated Admin dialogs do not duplicate imports.
why: Avoid the Zeta per-actor order bug; catalog known-issue entry gives this workaround.
workaround: Guest created with --index 0; Admin build passed.

what: Interim public landing on Customer: set supportGuestAccess=true and register a GuestPage (Trail Shop title and Login / Register button), while the Guest actor was blocked.
why: Catalog Guest Page entry gives the documented way; user had asked for a public actor, so this is a stop-gap.

what: Admin home: register AdminHome as the DashboardPage visual element, which redirects / to the Dashboard view, instead of editing generated routes.
why: Catalog Dashboard Page entry: an empty dashboard renders the DashboardPage visual element; Customer already does the same with CatalogHome.

what: Give ImportRunInfo.undo its own output TO (UndoMessage) to clear the duplicate import, and change UndoCustomImplementation to return UndoMessage.
why: Builder read the shared output type as the trigger; catalog says a shared output alone did not reproduce it, so this is a workaround with an unproven cause.
workaround: Model change plus Java change; build -i passed; commit e4897a7.

what: Guest products access is read-only and derived: DERIVED getter webshop::Product!filter(p | p.active) on GuestProductInfo (name, sku, price, unit, description).
why: Show only active products to the public; keep the public TO minimal.

what: The Guest actor reuses the ShopProductInfo transfer object through an access instead of its own GuestProductInfo transfer object.
why: The first version with GuestProductInfo was replaced: the shop search and boughtTogether operations then work for the anonymous actor with no token (POST /api/webshop/Guest/ShopProductInfo/search returned 200).

what: Customer front-end parts were copied into the Guest module instead of shared through a package, so a change to the shop home must be made in two places.
why: The two frontends are separate modules. The builder says the catalog recommends sharing through a package but did not try it.
workaround: Copy, with a note in GAPS (R19-18a).

what: On the Guest app, Add to cart and Login to buy do not put items in a cart. They send the visitor to /webshop/Customer/ to sign in.
why: A guest cannot buy; payment needs the Customer login.
